Soroche, altitude sickness, gives no warning. It can arrive on your first night in Cusco, at 3,400 meters, and take away the day you were so looking forward to. That's why we factor it in from the moment we design your trip, not as a warning in the fine print.
Si vuelas directo de Lima a Cusco, tu cu: If you fly straight from Lima to Cusco, your body goes from sea level to 3,400 meters in just over an hour. That's why the order of the days matters as much as the places.
En El Perú completo, nuestro journey de: On The Complete Peru, our 14-day journey, you don't land in Cusco all at once: first you pass through Arequipa (2,335 m), the Colca Canyon and Lake Titicaca. When you reach Cusco, on day 8, your body already knows the altitude.
En los journeys de 9 y 10 días vuelas a: On the 9- and 10-day journeys you fly to Cusco on day 3 and the next day you go down to the Sacred Valley, about 600 meters lower. After Machu Picchu you have a free day in Cusco, before the highest hikes.
Queremos que tu primer día en los Andes: We want your first day in the Andes to be yours, not your headache's.
El cuerpo se adapta solo si le das tiemp: Your body adapts on its own if you give it time. This is what we recommend to every traveler:
El primer día, sin caminatas largas ni e: On the first day, no long hikes or rushing up stairs.

La laguna Humantay (unos 4.200 m) y Vini: Humantay Lake (about 4,200 m) and Vinicunca, Rainbow Mountain (above 5,000 m), are the highest points of our journeys. That's why they always come after several days at altitude, never right after landing.

De mayo a septiembre es la temporada sec: From May to September is the dry season: clear skies, mild days and cold nights. From December to March it rains, and in February the Inca Trail closes for maintenance.

Te recogemos en el aeropuerto. Por la ta: We pick you up at the airport. In the afternoon you explore Lima's historic center, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and its markets, tasting 12 Peruvian bites. To finish, a pisco sour if you feel like it.
Lancha a las islas Ballestas, hogar de l: Boat to the Ballestas Islands, home to sea lions and Humboldt penguins, passing the Candelabra, a giant drawing in the sand whose origin nobody knows for sure. Lunch at a pisco vineyard and dune buggies with sandboarding in Huacachina until sunset.
Vuelo a Arequipa y recorrido privado por: Flight to Arequipa and a private tour of its colonial center, built with sillar, a white volcanic stone: that's why it's called the White City. In the background, the Misti volcano.
Cruzas los Andes hacia el cañón del Colc: You cross the Andes to the Colca Canyon, almost twice as deep as the Grand Canyon, and end the day in hot springs. Night in Chivay.
Desde el mirador del Colca ves planear a: From the Colca viewpoint you watch the Andean condor glide, with a wingspan of up to three meters. Then, the road to Puno, gateway to Titicaca.
Navegas el Titicaca, el lago navegable m: You sail Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world: first the floating islands of the Uros, handmade from totora reeds, then Amantaní, where you have dinner and sleep in the home of a local family.
Isla de Taquile, donde los hombres tejen: Taquile Island, where the men knit and the textiles are recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage. At night, bus to Cusco.
Recorrido privado por Cusco, la capital: Private tour of Cusco, capital of the Inca Empire, where you'll see Inca walls beneath colonial churches. To finish, its viewpoints.
Las salineras de Maras, que se trabajan: The Maras salt pans, worked since before the Incas; the circular terraces of Moray; the textiles of Chinchero; and Ollantaytambo, an Inca town that is still inhabited. In the afternoon, panoramic train to Aguas Calientes.
Machu Picchu con guía privado: la ciudad: Machu Picchu with a private guide: the 15th-century Inca citadel, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. Return by train and private transfer to Cusco.
Caminata a Vinicunca, la Montaña de Colo: Hike to Vinicunca, Rainbow Mountain, above 5,000 m: its stripes come from the minerals in the earth. At night, bus to Puerto Maldonado.
Navegas el río Tambopata hasta el lodge,: You sail the Tambopata River to the lodge, in one of the most biodiverse places on the planet. Guided jungle walk and a night outing to see monkeys, caimans and birds.
Al amanecer, cientos de loros y guacamay: At dawn, hundreds of parrots and macaws arrive at the Chuncho clay lick to eat clay. Then, lakes and jungle trails.
